minutes_text:
AGENDA
  COMMISSION ON THE STATUS OF WOMEN
  COUNCIL CHAMBERS
  613 E. Broadway, 2nd Floor
  Glendale, CA 91206

  MAY 8, 2023 AT 4:05 PM

1.  ROLL CALL
  PRESENT: Commissioners Broussalian, Khojayan, Lambillotte, Tatiyants, Ex
  Officio Roth and Ex Officio Gonzalez
  ABSENT: Commissioner Perian

2.  REGULAR BUSINESS AGENDA

a.  Report of Recorder, re: Posting of Agenda. The Agenda for the May 8, 2023
  Regular Meeting of the Commission on the Status of Women was Posted
  on Thursday, May 4, 2023 on the Bulletin Board Outside City Hall.
3.  INTRODUCTIONS AND PRESENTATIONS

a.  Presentation: Sexual Assault Mock Bill by YMCA Young Legislatures,
  Mallory Apy, Nicole LaHendro, and Chelsea Lawrence

  Director of Programs at the YMCA of the Foothills, Chelsea Lawrence stated that
  she is leading the youth and government program for 9th to 12th graders. Nicole
  LaHendro stated that she served as the bill chair for the YMCA of the Foothills
  Youth and Government delegation. LaHendro stated she wrote the bills and
  helped delegates draft bill ideas. Youth and Government is a model legislature in
  court that enables high school students to learn about civil engagement and
  experience government policy making. Students have the opportunity to
  participate at the legislative houses and brainstorm mock bill ideas to either
  change a bill, add on to an existing bill or create a new bill. Mallory Apy spoke
  about a mock bill that she authored in the model legislature regarding a needed
  change in the way in which the California National Guard investigates sexual
  assault cases. She stated that this is a prevalent problem across the country.
  Apy gave an example of a United States Army soldier, Vanessa Guillén who was
  sexually assaulted. The perpetrator of her assault was not disciplined and she
  was eventually murdered. Apy stated that we need this bill to create change and
   justice for victims of sexual assault. Chair Lambillotte asked for more information
  about the program and the response was that the program begins in September
  and meets on a weekly basis. Apy stated that part of the program is the student
  legislative body which drafts the mock bills around November then the bills are
  taken to Sacramento legislature for vote to pass or deny the bills. Student Ex
  Officio Roth stated that she was in the program for three years and asked if the
  bill has moved forward. Apy’s response was that the bill is in its early stages and
  that she is working on moving the bill forward to Sacramento. Chair Lambillotte
  stated that the Commission has relationships and can help get in touch with
  Assembly member Laura Friedman, Senator Portantino, and Adam Schiff’s
  offices. Commissioner Tatiyants asked how Apy became interested in the topic
  and the response was that she became interested after watching the
  documentary called “I am Vanessa Guillén”. Student Ex Officio Gonzalez asked
  how an individual can join the program and the response was that a meeting is
  held at the beginning of the school year for new delegates who are interested in
  joining.

b.  Presentation: GUSD Yellow Ribbon Week Update by GUSD Director, Hagop
  Eulmessekian

  Director of Student Support Services for GUSD, Hagop Eulmessekian spoke
  about Yellow Ribbon Week held every January during the week of Martin Luther
  King Jr. Day. Eulmessekian stated there are two events held by GUSD which
  are Red Ribbon Week and Yellow Ribbon Week. Red Ribbon Week focuses on
  having drug free campuses and Yellow Ribbon Week focuses on school safety
  and kindness. He also stated that GUSD is trying to bring back Hands and
  Words Are Not for Hurting Campaign this year. Chair Lambillotte stated that the
  Commission on the Status of Women purchased the materials for the school
  district to implement the program. Eulmessekian thanked the Commission for the
  donation. Student Ex Officio Roth asked if there are any counselors provided by
  the school district to students and the response was that the number of
  counselors that have been hired by GUSD has increased tremendously.
  Commissioner Broussalian asked if there is a lot of parent involvement in GUSD
  and the response was that there is more parent involvement in elementary
  schools than in middle and high schools. Eulmessekian stated that parents are
  always welcome to join the Parent Teacher Association.

4.  ORAL COMMUNICATIONS
  Discussion is limited to items NOT a part of this agenda. Each speaker is allowed
  5 minutes. The Commission may question or respond to the speaker but there
  will be no debate or discussion. Staff may refer the matter to the proper
  department for investigation and report.
  No public comments.
 5.  CONSENT ITEMS

a.  Approval of the minutes of the regular Commission Meeting held on
  February 13, 2023

  Motion by Commissioner Tatiyants and seconded by Khojayan
  Ayes: Commissioner Broussalian, Khojayan, Tatiyants, and Chair Lambillottee
  Noes:
  Absent: Commissioner Perian
  Abstain:
  Motion passes (4-0-1-0)

6.  ACTION ITEMS

a.  Request for Proclamation from the Glendale City Council Designating June
  2023 as Pride Month
  1. Motion Requesting a Proclamation from Glendale City Council
  Designating June 2023 as Pride Month
  Motion by Commissioner Tatiyants and seconded by Khojayan
  Ayes: Commissioner Broussalian, Khojayan, Tatiyants, and Chair Lambillottee
  Noes:
  Absent: Commissioner Perian
  Abstain:
  Motion passes (4-0-1-0)

b.  Update Ad Hoc Committees to Support the 2023-26 Strategic Plan for the
  Commission on the Status of Women
  1. Motion Providing Further Direction on Ad Hoc Committees
  Motion by Commissioner Broussalian to establish three Ad Hoc Committees
  (Evaluate and Assess, Policy Development, Advocacy and Advising, and
  Education, Awareness and Outreach) and dissolve the current four Ad Hoc
  Committees. Seconded by Tatiyants.

  Ayes: Commissioner Broussalian, Khojayan, Tatiyants, and Chair Lambillottee
  Noes:
  Absent: Commissioner Perian
  Abstain:
  Motion passes (4-0-1-0)
   Motion by Commissioner Tatiyants to assign Commissioner Broussalian and
  Chair Lambillotte to the Evaluate and Assess Committee, assign Commissioner
  Perian, Chair Lambillotte, and Student Ex Officio Roth to the Policy Development,
  Advocacy and Advising Committee and assign Commissioner Tatiyants,
  Commissioner Khojayan, Student Ex Officio Roth and Student Ex Officio
  Gonzalez to the Education, Awareness and Outreach Committee. Seconded by
  Broussalian.

  Ayes: Commissioner Broussalian, Khojayan, Tatiyants, and Chair Lambillottee
  Noes:
  Absent: Commissioner Perian
  Abstain:
  Motion passes (4-0-1-0)

c.  Legislative Update
  1. Motion Providing Direction on State Legislation
  Motion by Commissioner Tatiyants to support all six bills. Seconded by Khojayan.

  Ayes: Commissioner Broussalian, Khojayan, Tatiyants, and Chair Lambillottee
  Noes:
  Absent: Commissioner Perian
  Abstain:
  Motion passes (4-0-1-0)

7.  HEARING

a.  Public Hearing for the 2023-2026 Strategic Plan

  Hearing opened at 5:16 p.m. and closed at 5:17 p.m.

  No public comments.
8.  REPORTS-INFORMATION ONLY

9.  COMMISSION ON THE STATUS OF WOMEN/STAFF COMMENTS
  City Clerk, Suzie Abajian stated that the report on the Status of Women is under
  way and that she and Chair Lambillotte have been working closely with the Mount
  Saint Mary’s University and providing extensive feedback on multiple revisions.
  Abajian stated that the final report will be discussed at the next Commission
  meeting. Abajian stated that the grant the city received by the California
  Commission on the Status of Women and Girls requires the Commission to hold
  a public hearing for that item. Abajian also mentioned that the City Clerk’s Office
  is in the process of hiring an analyst who will be assisting with the operations of
  the Commission on the Status of Women as well as other projects within the City
  Clerk’s Office. Lastly, Abajian stated that she received a correspondence from the
   California Commission on the Status of Women and Girls to inform workers about
  pay transparency SB1162 regarding equal pay in California. The California
  Commission is asking the public to complete a survey which can be found on the
  Commission on the Status of Women website and closes on May 12, 2023 at
  noon. Chair Lambillotte stated that the 2023-2026 Strategic Plan has been
  approved by the commission and is going to be presented to City Council in the
  coming weeks. Student Ex Officio Roth provided an update regarding her project
  at the Glendale Library.

10. ADJOURNMENT AT 5:38 PM
  Motion by Commissioner Broussalian and seconded by Khojayan.
